result:
I used "Tom" as the new subject: the speaker starts "Tom forgot", stops, and restarts with "I forgot". The gold subject "I" (`person.n.01 EQU speaker`) is a placeholder concept, so the wrong subject is a named person, `male.n.02 Name "Tom"`. No new WordNet sense was needed, so I didn't run a lookup.

**Gold concept positions:**

| Position | Concept |
|---|---|
| 0 | `person.n.01` EQU speaker (the subject) |
| 1 | `forget.v.02` |
| 2 | `time.n.08` |
| 3 | `person.n.01` |
| 4 | `email.n.01` |
| 5 | `address.n.02` |

**Repaired SBN concept positions:**

| Position | Concept and edges |
|---|---|
| 0 | `entity.n.01` (anchor, ⑤) |
| | `CORRECTION <1` |
| 1 | `male.n.02 Name "Tom" EQU -1` → points to the anchor |
| 2 | `forget.v.02 Agent -1 Time +1` (Theme dropped, ①) |
| 3 | `time.n.08 TPR now` |
| | `CONJUNCTION <2` |
| 4 | `person.n.01 EQU speaker EQU -4` → points to the anchor |
| 5 | `forget.v.02 Agent -1 Time +1 Theme +4` → Theme lands on `address.n.02` at 9 |
| 6 | `time.n.08 TPR now` |
| 7 | `person.n.01 EQU speaker` |
| 8 | `email.n.01` |
| 9 | `address.n.02 User -2 Theme -1` |

**Checks:**
- **Indices:** every index lands on the intended concept.
- **R2 and R3:** nothing points into the `CORRECTION` box from outside. The reparandum only points back to the anchor or within its own box.
- **R5:** the reparandum is connected to the anchor through `EQU -1`.
- **R6:** there are no separators after the repair, so no box pointers needed updating.
